# Step AC: small fixes from the review

Lex (2026-11-16, Orbit TOOLS-315, pick 5 of the TOOLS-296 review): the review's small fixes and low bugs that steps Y to AB did not already fix, in Lex's order; the flaky "New script" step of the B-roll browser check (TOOLS-309); and two follow-ups from step AA if cheap. Bug fixes and work behind the scenes: no prototype. One change shows on screen (a browser copy left behind no longer shows in the switcher).

## What it does

- **TOOLS-309, the flaky browser check.** `smoke-broll-lazy.mjs`'s "another new script" step (1280 px, after a refused module load) timed out now and then, on live with an older browser profile and in some full runs. Reproduced on live with a copy of the saved older profile: the script menu draws its list a frame after it opens (17-18 ms), which moves "Open a script…" and "New script" down a row; the check found "New script" in the frame before and its press landed on "Open a script…" (the menu closed and no new script came). One frame is too soon for a person to act on, so this is the check's own problem, not the editor's. The check now waits for this open's list (the open script is the current row, and "New script" stays put for two frames) and presses 150 ms after finding the spot, as a slow machine would, so it fails every run without the wait. The other suites already click those items with a script click after waiting (`smoke-saving`, `smoke-rare-parts`). `smoke-saving`'s two-tab run failed the same way on the start screen (4 of 6 runs, also on `origin/dev`): "Reopen …" joins the centred row a moment after the screen shows and moves "Open a script"; it now waits until that button stays put.
- **A browser copy that can't be deleted after Save as** (review bug, step AA follow-up). When a browser script moves to a file and the browser refuses to delete its copy, the copy's name is kept in local storage (`script-editor:movedCopies`, `createLeftCopies` in `saving.js`): the switcher leaves it out, no script takes its name while it is there (also with the moved file taken off the switcher; review round 1, P2: before, a new script could take the name and the next listing deleted it), and the next listing (the start screen, or opening the switcher) deletes it, unless it was saved into since (another tab still had the script open): then it shows again with those words, on the listing that finds it. **A copy in use is never deleted** (PR #75's second look, P0): every tab holds a Web Lock under the script's name (`script-editor:script:<name>`, shared) for as long as it has that browser script open (`copies.open`, called when a script opens, moves, is renamed or is saved into the browser), and every save into a browser script holds it from its first step to the end of its write (`files.held` in `createSaving`, also the save of a script the person just left and saves that waited; a file on the computer is saved without it). The move to a file and every later cleanup delete a copy only under that lock held alone, taken only when it is free at once: a copy open in a tab, or being saved into, is skipped and stays kept by name; a save that comes during a delete waits for it and then finds no file, so the tab shows "Not saved" or keeps a draft, and no words land in a file about to be deleted. What is kept with a name is the fingerprint of the copy's words as the moving tab last wrote or read them (handed over by Save as; first built with the copy's file time, replaced as the next point tells), so words another tab saved before the move are never taken for the script that moved: such a copy stays a browser script. A copy that can't be read once stays kept and is tried again on the next listing. Limits, all on the safe side: a tab still running the editor from before this change holds no lock, so it behaves as before (a move in another tab deletes the copy and that tab's next save shows "Not saved"); a tab that opens a script in the same instant another tab moves it may get its lock after the delete, and then shows "Not saved" too; a name kept without a fingerprint shows again instead of being deleted; while a tab has a kept copy open, its own switcher lists it as the open script (without the Browser tag) and the agent's list of recent scripts leaves it out, until the tab leaves it. Cleanups run one at a time across tabs (`navigator.locks`; where a browser has no Web Locks, `tabLocks` in `saving.js` stands in for them inside the tab) and read the name again before the delete; a name is freed only when its copy is gone when looked up inside the lock, so two listings at once (or two tabs) never delete a script that took the freed name (GPT second look, release review); a full listing frees the names whose copy went some other way (an older tab, cleared storage; review round 4). Before, the failure was ignored and the copy stayed in the switcher with the Browser tag.
- **Unchanged is decided by a script's words, and saves into one browser script run one at a time** (PR #75's second look on 8158156, P0 and P2; Lex's card TOOLS-315, 5c). Before, a tab knew a file by the time it read after its own write. With one browser script open in two tabs, the other tab's save could land between a tab's write and that read: the tab then held the other tab's file time for its own words, its changed-on-disk check saw nothing, and its later move to a file took the copy for the script that moved and deleted the other tab's words. Three changes at the root:
  - *Fingerprint.* What a tab knows of a file is the words it last wrote into it or read from it (`savedText`); `fingerprint` in `saving.js` is their SHA-256 (as the file gives them back, UTF-8: half of a character pair as the replacement character the file gets, and no byte-order mark in front, so a script an agent hands over with one is no changed file; the second look on a172820, P3). The changed-on-disk check (`diskConflict`) reads the file on every save and compares words, whatever the file's time (also a file with the same or an older time, and a script opened without one); the move to a file hands the cleanup those words (`placed(handle, { was, words })`, `afterMove(name, words)`), and a copy left behind is kept with their fingerprint (`script-editor:movedCopyPrints`; never the words). A copy is the script that moved only when it holds exactly those words. A name kept without a fingerprint (by an earlier build of this step, which kept a file time; that build never went live) is never deleted: its copy shows again. The file's time is only shown (a draft's day, the prompter link); the save queue's requests carry no file time any more, and `changedOnDisk` left `save-queue.js`.
  - *One save at a time.* Every save into a browser script holds a second Web Lock alone (`script-editor:write:<name>`, inside the shared one that keeps cleanups away) from its look at the file to the end of its write, the read of the file's time included. Two tabs' saves into one script run one after the other; the second then finds the first's words and shows "The file changed on disk" instead of writing over them. A new script (`copies.create`) looks up its name and writes under the same lock, so two tabs that take one free name at the same moment make one script and the other tab is told; a script that follows its title (`copies.rename`) takes a name only when no file has it, looked up under that name's lock, and leaves a name another tab is writing under for its next save. A new script left as it came (`copies.discard`) is deleted only while no other tab has it open or saves into it and it still holds the words it came with (before, another tab could have opened it and typed into it). A file on the computer has no such lock (other programs write it too); the changed-on-disk check is its guard. The lock goes by the file's own name as the save asks for it (its handle's): a save that waited while the script followed its title to another name, for a script the person then left, holds the new name, as the other tabs do, and a draft it has to keep goes by that name too (the second look on a172820, P0: it held the old name, so another tab's save into the renamed script ran alongside and was written over without a word).
  - *Every freed copy is listed.* A listing leaves out the files whose name is kept. After its cleanup, every file it left out whose name is free then is a row (`shown`, read under the cleanups' lock): a copy with other words, freed by this listing or by another one at the same moment, and a new script that took a freed name. Before, of two listings at once of a copy with newer words, one showed it and the other did not until the switcher opened again.
- **A waiting Ctrl+S without a file** (step AA follow-up). The demo's Ctrl+S made while its Save as wrote waited with no file of its own; when another script without a file opened before the write ended, it ran on that script, saving it into the browser and renaming it. Now, when another script opens, a waiting click without a file is dropped: its words are in the draft the app keeps on leaving (they come back as "Unsaved changes" when that script is opened again), which is as new or newer, or the app found nothing unsaved (GPT second look and review round 4: a draft written by the click could hide words typed after it, or bring back words the person had taken out).
- **Facts written once for the Worker and the tab.** The agent token's eight hours and the "No asks yet" answer are in `public/agent-link.js` (new, 469 bytes), which `app.js` and `worker/mcp.js` import; the Worker takes the room id and key patterns from `public/together/link.js` and the room protocol from `public/together/room.js`, as it already did for the room's keep time.
- **One HTML escape.** `escHtml` lives in `doc.js`; `app.js` and `broll.js` use it instead of their own copies (a missing value now escapes to nothing, never "null").
- **No dead code.** `applyBrollChanges`, used only by tests, is gone; the tests use `applyBrollChangesReport(...).markdown` as the app does.
- **A cap on the MCP request body** (review, info). `/mcp` refuses a body bigger than the largest allowed call (`unmark_cue`'s cueIds with their block ids, which hold at most twice a script's words since cues overlap only where bold sits inside a link inside bold, with a 500-character quote on every cue, every character spelled as `\uXXXX`, plus 64 KB: 2,566,336 bytes) with 413 before reading it in full, by its stated length or while it streams. `unmark_cue` takes cueIds holding up to that many characters per call and asks the agent to split a bigger batch, as the 413 does (a file opened from disk may be longer than an agent-sized script; second look on PR #73; the second look on PR #73 found overlapping cueIds from `list_cues` that a one-script limit refused; release review: its second look found a long-cueId call the first cap refused; Claude's review then found a 36 MB cap gave the protection away). `readUpTo` moved to `mcp.js`, so the picture upload and MCP read bodies the same way.
- **Module names.** The app's modules import each other as `Doc`, `Changes`, `Links`, `Cues`, `Broll` and `SaveQueue` instead of `D`, `C`, `L`, `K`, `B` and `Q` (`app.js`, `changes.js`, `together-adapter.js`, `broll-app.js`, `saving.js`).
- **History comments.** The examples the review named in `cues.js` and `press.js` now say what the code does instead of how it was first built.
- Sizes: the files the page needs before it runs went from 15 files and 429,605 bytes (at a100cf2, this step's base on `dev`) to 16 files and 436,301 bytes (+6,696: `agent-link.js`, the longer module names, the browser-copy code), and to 441,992 bytes with the locks for copies in use (+5,691, in `saving.js` and `app.js`), and to 447,326 bytes with the fingerprint and the lock for saves (+5,334, in `saving.js`; `app.js` and `save-queue.js` shrank).

## Declined

- Comments with dated choices (`Lex, 2026-…`, step names): kept. `AGENTS.md` makes Lex's dated choices the reference, and the comments point to them; only the review's named history examples changed.
- `sketchSvg` in `broll-app.js` and `sketchHtml` in `broll.js`: not one helper. The frames take sketches that were cleaned when they came in and are not draggable; `sketchHtml` cleans again for the storyboard file. One helper would clean every frame on every draw.
- The two SHA-256 functions: the tab's is synchronous on purpose (the host handles room messages in order); the Worker uses the platform's `crypto.subtle`.
- The one-at-a-time queues written three ways, and the text-node walks in `app.js` and `together/carets.js`: each guards different state; making them one is a refactor, not a small fix.
- `isBrollAnswer` "inlined" in `together-adapter.js`: those checks are a different rule (selection asks that are not B-roll, whatever their status).
- The same limit checked in the Worker and the tab (sketch length): the review calls it defence in depth; both read the same constant from `broll.js`.
- The silent `.catch` on the recent list's queue (`updateRecent`): it keeps the queue going; a refused write leaves the switcher without that entry, as with storage turned off, which the editor treats as normal and shows nowhere.
- Old picture files left in `pictures/` after shots are removed: Lex chose to keep them (2026-11-16, saving try-out "old pictures kept").
- The agent token in local storage: the Content-Security-Policy of step Y is the review's suggested answer; it is live.
